clue.text: Flock angering coot up in the air

indicators.note: something up in the air is unsettled and all over the place, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A flock of birds rises into the air after a coot makes them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' looks like birds beside the coot, but here it is a church's people.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregation is the body of worshippers in a church, often called the pastor's flock.

clue.text: Lessons about girls

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Lessons covering the subject of girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes are teaching sessions, the periods in which pupils have lessons.

clue.text: Illustrious, upsetting Twitter owner penning book

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the turned name holds the book letter
upsetting in a down clue turns the name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Elon Musk bought Twitter in 2022

explanation.surface: An illustrious figure is upset because the Twitter owner has written a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means distinguished and grand in character or rank, as an illustrious person is.

clue.text: I urge oil reforms and Sunak's initially unswerving

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again into a new order
initially takes the first letter of Sunak's

parts.note: first letter of Sunak's

explanation.surface: Someone urges oil-industry reforms, and Prime Minister Rishi Sunak is at first unbending about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister 2022–24.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious can mean scrupulous and unfailingly devoted, as in doing something religiously every day.

clue.text: Sales rep not a man of refinement

indicators.note: not a means the letter A is taken away from the word for the rep

parts.note: a sales agent represents a firm

explanation.surface: The salesman is no gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gent, short for gentleman, is a well-mannered, cultured man.

clue.text: Conservatives going round the man's premises

indicators.note: going round means the party members encircle the word for the man

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
he is the man; the 's reads as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Conservatives visit and walk around the man's premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premises' looks like a building, but here it means ideas assumed as the basis for an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises are propositions put forward as a basis for reasoning, so hypotheses.

clue.text: Monet fortunately picked up frames on a regular basis

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the letters read from bottom to top
frames means the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Luckily, someone collected Monet paintings in frames on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening many times.

clue.text: Game sick people mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned says the word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: patients are sick people under medical care

explanation.surface: A game for invalids is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the card game played alone, known as solitaire in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a single-player card game, the British name for solitaire.

clue.text: Almost November and ahead of time

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: Nearly November and things are running early.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means not quite, by a small margin.

clue.text: A male tramp cut with weapon — this might be needed

parts.note: A as written, plus M, the standard abbreviation for male

indicators.note: cut here means docked of its last letter, so the word for tramp loses its tail

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A man stabs a vagrant with a lance, and someone had better call for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: after a stabbing like this, the vehicle in question might be needed.
explanation.definitionFit: After a man is wounded with a weapon, an emergency vehicle to take him to hospital would be called.

clue.text: Drinks with English guy

definitions.note: as a verb, to guy is to mock or make fun of

parts.note: teas are drinks

explanation.surface: Someone has drinks with an English man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man, but it is the verb meaning to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to poke fun at them, which is to rib or mock them playfully.

clue.text: Sledge cut to pieces, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for cutting to pieces is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to slay is to kill violently, to cut to pieces

explanation.surface: A sledge is smashed to bits, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge, a vehicle on runners pulled over snow.

clue.text: Boldness that is preceding cricketer's last boundary

indicators.note: preceding places the earlier pieces before the cricketer's final letter

parts.note: front can mean nerve or effrontery, as in 'he had the front to ask'
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'id est', that is

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the last letter of cricketer

explanation.surface: A cricketer's boldness lets him score one last boundary, a hit to the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a scoring hit to the edge of the field; here it is the border of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the border line between two countries, a boundary.

clue.text: Jack so right to conceal distress

indicators.note: to conceal means the pair of words wraps around and hides the word for distress

parts.note: taken as written
to ail is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: Jack is quite right to hide his distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is old slang for a seaman, as in jack tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack, or jack tar, is an old informal word for a seaman in the navy.

clue.text: One criticised about Oscar getting separated

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means the word for criticised goes round the Oscar letter

parts.note: slated means harshly criticised
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone panned for winning an Oscar is cut off from colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means set apart or cut off from others.

clue.text: Look after European and cry, regularly showing bias

parts.note: to tend is to look after

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words and cry

parts.note: every second letter of these words

explanation.surface: A carer and a European burst into tears, revealing prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is an inclination or leaning, so a bias towards one thing.

clue.text: Lousy nuts deter apes

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Awful nuts are enough to put off apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food apes might reject; it signals the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate can mean extremely bad, as in a desperate performance, so terrible.

clue.text: Hold spellbound, mouth opening

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put in a trance, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a way in, as the mouth or opening of a cave

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to captivate; an entrance is a doorway or way in.

clue.text: Angry at home before grand voyage

indicators.note: before puts the first words ahead of the grand piece

parts.note: cross means angry
in means at home
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone stays home in a temper before setting off on a great trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossing is a journey across the sea, such as a ferry or ship's passage.

clue.text: Nice Bordeaux?

parts.note: Nice and Bordeaux are both large towns in France, read as a pair of examples

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a good claret; the question mark warns that Nice is the Riviera resort, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and Bordeaux are examples of large French urban centres.

clue.text: Numb martial artist swallowed by snake

indicators.note: swallowed by puts the martial artist inside the snake

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Bruce Lee was the famous martial artist

explanation.surface: A martial artist goes numb after being swallowed whole by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that is asleep has lost feeling, as when pins and needles set in.

clue.text: Irons robes softly for daughter

indicators.note: softly for daughter means the softly letter takes the daughter letter's place

parts.note: dresses are robes or gowns
P is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone gently irons a daughter's robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them flat with a hot iron.

clue.text: Area over river by small farm vehicles

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Little farm vehicles cross an area beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractors are the powered vehicles that pull ploughs and trailers on a farm.

clue.text: Songbird — the French book might have this on the cover

definitions.text: book might have this on the cover

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French book's cover features a picture of a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's name is printed on its front, so the cover carries it.

clue.text: Drop terribly crude joke finally

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of crude are rearranged
finally takes only the final letter of the word joke

parts.note: last letter of joke

explanation.surface: A comedian is told to drop a terribly crude joke at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something is to lower or cut it, to make it drop.

clue.text: Relative's dirty article removed

indicators.note: removed means the article is taken out of the word for dirty

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A relative's grubby piece of clothing has been taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, the brother of a parent.

clue.text: Some truth in this clue

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: There is some truth in this clue, the setter admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a suggestion or pointer, the job of a crossword clue.

clue.text: Calm thoroughbred's first horse-riding competition

parts.note: even can mean calm and steady, as in an even temper

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of thoroughbred

parts.note: first letter of thoroughbred

explanation.surface: A calm thoroughbred takes part in its first riding contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian discipline of dressage, cross-country and jumping; a single such contest is an event.

clue.text: Drunk causes inn problems

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk causes trouble at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuisances are annoyances, things that cause bother and trouble.

clue.text: Still shaking, steel nerves outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters go around the hospital letter
shaking suggests jumbling, so the letters of steel nerves are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital is still shaking despite having nerves of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' sounds like an adjective for keeping steady, but it is the adverb meaning all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning however or in spite of that.
